original_test_intent: Inject a correctable MP1/SMU firmware error at the intended socket and index, verify exactly one fresh correctable report without reset or service loss, then confirm SMU-controlled telemetry, power and thermal functions remain healthy.
original_method: Identify the MP1/SMU firmware block and errorindex0 meaning; validate all tuple flags and socket coverage; preserve logs and raw settings; run one approved CE; correlate tool output with a fresh MP1-specific MCA/CPER/WHEA event; assert no reset and no UCE escalation; verify sensor, clock/power/thermal-control and firmware responsiveness; restore BIOS/HDT state.
manual_activity: The FAE resolves the GMI3 script mismatch, approves the MP1/SMU index and tuple, performs the single CE injection, monitors firmware services and restores RAS/HDT settings.
required_inputs: MP1/SMU block and errorindex0 definition plus socket/package coverage
Vendor semantics for errormode1, enablemcapolling0 and errortype0
Decision whether the GMI3 script URL is erroneous, relevant or a required separate artifact
Exact CE source/severity/count fields and explicit no-reset/no-UCE oracle
Supported OS and timeout plus SMU telemetry, thermal, power and clock health limits
FFE threshold relevance, debug-disable interaction, aborts, recovery and raw restoration
safety_requirements: Dedicated monitored SUT with independent console and stable thermal/power margin
Baseline SMU sensors, clock/power/thermal controls and logs without destroying prior evidence
Inject once only after firmware/index and command identity approval
Abort on reset, UCE, sensor loss, power/thermal control anomaly, firmware timeout or unexpected event source
No automatic retry; restore all BIOS/HDT/debug/threshold settings and revalidate services
agent_execution_scope: Validate source script identity, tuple semantics, CE oracle, timeout and firmware-health plan
Collect read-only platform identity, settings, logs, CPER/MCA/WHEA/SEL and SMU telemetry/control health
Do not choose index/socket/mode, alter BIOS/HDT, inject, reset, recover, retry or issue verdict
engineer_actions: Approve MP1 tuple and socket coverage
Supervise injection and firmware-service health checks

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Perform a source-identified MP1 CE with exactly-one-event/no-reset acceptance and before/after firmware-service telemetry.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds script identity reconciliation, block/index decoding, multi-socket applicability, CE count/severity, negative UCE/reset checks and SMU service health.

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Master Script points to a GMI3-correctable path despite MP1/SMU identity. Index0 and mode flags are undocumented, socket0 coverage is unexplained, the UCE/BERT Criteria branch has no applicability rule, and CE timeout/service-health acceptance is incomplete.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The intended MP1 CE and literal tuple are clear enough for static review. The mismatches gate execution but do not prevent recording the review.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row 81 Wistron-System RAS-00801-V003: reconcile the GMI3-correctable Script URL with MP1/SMU coverage; define MP1 block/errorindex0, socket coverage and smupsp errormode1/enablemcapolling0/errortype0 semantics; state whether UCE/BERT Criteria is escalation-only; specify exact fresh CE/no-reset evidence, SMU telemetry/power/thermal/clock health, FFE/debug-setting relevance, OS timeout, aborts and restoration.

review_improvement: Exposes the unrelated script identity and adds an MP1-specific exactly-one-CE/no-reset contract plus firmware-control health rather than accepting a generic corrected log.
independent_technical_reasoning: MP1 is the SMU controller, so a nominally correctable injected event can affect firmware services even when Linux continues running. The linked script name references GMI3, which could drive a different injection path. Errorindex0 and mcapolling mode require vendor decoding, and acceptance must include no reset/UCE escalation plus continued sensor, thermal and power control—not just tool PASS.
